source.text: A lumped plate per slice, started at its steady state T_b + q_k/h and then cooled less and less well. Heat capacity per square metre 14010, surface 1. Slice 4 of 10 (the hottest, 77.573 kW/m) warms monotonically from 625.8576 K to 801.919 K at 40 s, which is the largest peak of the run. The tolerance 5.3 K is the sum, rounded up to 0.05 K, of 1 % of the rise (1.761 K), twice the bound on the heat the slices exchange along the height (rate 0.003333 /s, exchange number 0.133 over the run, bound 1.462 K, twice 2.925 K) and the internal rise of the hottest cell above the lumped mean (at most 0.586 K); fixed before any run.
source.check: Second method: FEED's independent finite-volume solution of every slice (tests/seedOracleStack.test.ts, the same bound added) and the real solver with FEED_SOLVER=1; FEED's own checks of the stack run (cross-check, energy balance, time step) all pass.

coverage.domain: synthetic plate with a conductivity of 400 W/m/K and a heat capacity of 3 MJ/m3/K (Biot number about 0.001) as 10 slices over 2 m with a cosine power shape, 50 kW per metre of height and width on average, each slice started from its own steady state at a film coefficient of 3000 W/m2/K, coolant 600 K, the film coefficient falling to 100 W/m2/K between 2 and 3 s (the loss of cooling of finding F17), 40 s
